# yt-dlp telemetry captures — Milestone 15

Captured on Linux with yt-dlp **2026.08.19**, aria2c **1.37.0** and local
FFmpeg, using generated three-second test media served over loopback HTTP.
No YouTube account, internet media or credentials were used. These are actual
stdout captures; stderr was empty. Tests replay them without a server/network.

- `native.txt`: native downloader, combined local MP4, WAV extraction.
- `aria2c.txt`: same media via aria2c, limited to 16 KiB/s, WAV extraction.
- `video.txt`: shared `build_youtube_video_command(180, destination=..., telemetry=True)`.
- `original.txt`: shared `build_youtube_audio_command(destination=..., telemetry=True)`.
- `wav.txt`: same audio builder with `wav=True`.

The last three used `--load-info-json` with two local HTTP formats: a 320x180
MP4 video-only stream and an M4A audio-only stream, generated by stream-copying
the combined test clip. Additional capture-only arguments were `--ignore-config`,
`--no-plugin-dirs`, `--no-cache-dir`, and `--limit-rate 32K`. Each command exited
zero and produced only the expected MP4, M4A or WAV in its own output directory.
They exercise real aria2c and FFmpeg, without depending on YouTube access.

Templates are defined verbatim in `ytdlp_progress.py`. Dictionary JSON projection
is intentional: optional values are omitted rather than interpolated as invalid
bare `NA` JSON. All records were newline-delimited; the parser also tests CR and
arbitrary chunk boundaries. Normal human messages and FILE paths are ignored.

Installed yt-dlp's `ExternalFD.real_download` emits a structured progress hook
only after aria2c exits successfully. Live aria2c readouts therefore use the
existing strict aria2 parser, enabled through GUI-only downloader arguments.
Native transfers expose JSON byte counts/speed/ETA while downloading. JSON
postprocessor hooks expose Merger, ExtractAudio, VideoRemuxer and MoveFiles stages.
The remuxer may find the file already MP4; starting the hook means entering that
postprocessor, not proof that a codec conversion or remux was necessary.

Percent is current-stream progress calculated from exact byte counts (or read
directly from aria2c). Estimates are not presented as exact totals. Postprocessing
clears transfer metrics; successful job completion depends on process exit.

References: [yt-dlp progress templates](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#verbosity-and-simulation-options)
and the installed executable's `yt_dlp/downloader/external.py` / postprocessor hooks.
